edges.mechanism: Metformin is renally cleared by tubular secretion and accumulates as kidney function falls, raising lactic acidosis risk. The label contraindicates eGFR <30, advises against starting at eGFR 30-45, and says to reassess below 45.
edges.evidence: Label; community cohort (n=75,413): acidosis HR 2.07 only at eGFR <30, no excess at 30-59; SR of CKD data

edges.mechanism: Acute or chronic metabolic acidosis, including DKA, is a label contraindication because of lactic acidosis risk.
edges.evidence: Prescribing label

edges.mechanism: Reduced lactate clearance; hepatic impairment is linked to lactic acidosis cases and use is not recommended.
edges.evidence: Prescribing label; no PK studies in hepatic impairment

edges.with: acute hypoxic states / surgery (e.g., acute heart failure, sepsis)
edges.mechanism: Hypoxia raises lactate production; the label lists hypoxic states, surgery and procedures as lactic acidosis risk factors.
edges.evidence: Prescribing label; 97% of 559 published lactic acidosis cases had independent risk factors

edges.mechanism: Contrast-induced kidney injury can cause metformin accumulation. Stop at or before contrast if eGFR is 30-60, with liver disease, alcoholism or heart failure, or with intra-arterial contrast; recheck eGFR at 48 h.
edges.evidence: Label; guideline review found conflicting recommendations based on level IV-V evidence

edges.mechanism: Alcohol potentiates metformin's effect on lactate metabolism; excessive intake is a lactic acidosis risk factor.
edges.evidence: Prescribing label

edges.mechanism: Cause non-anion-gap hyperchloremic metabolic acidosis and may increase lactic acidosis risk with metformin.
edges.evidence: Prescribing label (Table 2)

edges.mechanism: OCT2 inhibition reduces renal tubular secretion of metformin. Metformin AUC rose 79% with 50 mg daily and 145% with 50 mg twice daily; exposure was lower in obese women with HIV.
edges.evidence: Label; PK study in healthy volunteers (n=30); PK study in obese women with HIV (n=15)

edges.mechanism: OCT2/MATE inhibition. Ranolazine 1000 mg twice daily raised metformin AUC 1.79-fold; the authors advise not exceeding 1700 mg/d metformin.
edges.evidence: Label; two phase 1 PK studies in T2D

edges.mechanism: Inhibits hepatic OCT1 and renal OCT2. Metformin AUC +24% in healthy adults; pharmacovigilance and PBPK lactic acidosis signal in renal failure.
edges.evidence: Label; clinical DDI study (n=16); FAERS disproportionality + PBPK

edges.mechanism: Label-listed OCT2/MATE inhibitor that may raise metformin exposure and lactic acidosis risk.
edges.evidence: Prescribing label only

edges.mechanism: Additive glucose lowering; a lower insulin or sulfonylurea dose may be needed. Severe hypoglycemia was 2.2% with glimepiride added to metformin in GRADE.
edges.evidence: Label; large RCT (GRADE, n=5047)

edges.mechanism: Metformin impairs calcium-dependent ileal B12 absorption (deficiency OR 2.45; serum B12 about -64 pmol/L). B12 supplementation corrects levels; the label recommends B12 checks every 2-3 years.
edges.evidence: Label; MAs of observational studies and RCTs; small RCT of oral B12 in metformin users

edges.mechanism: Without B vitamins or folic acid, metformin raised homocysteine (MD +2.02 umol/L); with them homocysteine fell (MD -0.74).
edges.evidence: MA of RCTs (12 publications)

edges.mechanism: Oral calcium reversed the metformin-induced fall in holotranscobalamin by counteracting calcium-dependent ileal membrane antagonism.
edges.evidence: Small comparative study (n=21)

edges.mechanism: Berberine inhibits OCT1/OCT2/MATE1-mediated metformin transport and changes metformin PK in rats. Glucose lowering is additive.
edges.evidence: In vitro and rat PK studies; low-quality RCT MA of berberine with oral hypoglycemics; no human PK study

edges.mechanism: Complementary mechanisms (alpha-glucosidase inhibition plus hepatic/gut actions): the combination lowered FBG, 2-h glucose and HbA1c more than either alone. Watch GI tolerability and hypoglycemia.
edges.evidence: MA of RCTs (mostly Chinese); comparative MA

edges.mechanism: Metformin offset rapamycin-induced glucose intolerance in female HET3 mice; ITP mice on both drugs lived at least as long as on rapamycin alone.
edges.evidence: Mouse study only; no human data

edges.mechanism: Metformin use is associated with hypomagnesemia (OR 3.72), possibly from GI loss and TRPM6 effects; check Mg if symptomatic.
edges.evidence: Cohort study (n=1106); case and narrative review

edges.mechanism: No PK interaction is known. Metformin-associated B12 deficiency can cause anemia; evaluate anemia before attributing it to iron deficiency.
edges.evidence: Label hematologic monitoring advice; small MA of iron-deficiency anemia in metformin users

edges.mechanism: Metformin activates AMPK and blunts mTORC1 and mitochondrial adaptations. In older adults it reduced lean mass and thigh muscle gains with resistance training and attenuated VO2max and insulin-sensitivity gains with aerobic training.
edges.evidence: RCTs: MASTERS (n=94) and aerobic training trial (n=53)

edges.mechanism: Crosses into the fetal environment. Added to insulin in T2D pregnancy it improved glycemia but raised small-for-gestational-age risk (RR 1.96). Neurodevelopment and malformation MAs are reassuring.
edges.evidence: RCT (MiTy, n=502) with child follow-up; MAs

edges.mechanism: Metformin causes intense diffuse bowel (mainly colonic) FDG uptake that can obscure abdominal lesions. Stopping for 48 h reduces it, but distal colon uptake persists with holds under 72 h.
edges.evidence: Prospective study; RCT (n=90) of 24- vs 48-h holds; retrospective cohorts

edges.mechanism: ATM rs11212617 is associated with treatment success (OR 1.35); SLC22A1 reduced-function variants affect PK in some studies but not HbA1c response in GoDARTS; SLC2A2 rs8192675 C allele gives a larger glucose fall.
edges.evidence: GWAS with replication meta-analysis; cohort studies; SR; not used clinically
